syntax_error:
-- Look just before "{token}": a missing comma, an unclosed ' or ( , or a keyword from another database.
-- MySQL uses `backticks` for names and 'single quotes' for text; LIMIT offset, count is fine here.
unknown_table:
-- If it should exist: run the missing migration, or check you're connected to the right database:
SELECT DATABASE();
unknown_column: -- then use the real column name in the query
ambiguous_column:
-- Put the table (or its alias) in front of the column everywhere it appears:
SELECT t1.{column}, ... FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON ... WHERE t1.{column} = ...;
unknown_function: -- MySQL equivalents: STRING_AGG -> GROUP_CONCAT, COALESCE works, NOW() works, ILIKE -> LIKE (case-insensitive by default collation)
duplicate_key:
-- See the row that already has this value:
SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE <unique column> = '{value}';
fk_missing_parent:
-- Check the parent exists:
SELECT * FROM {parent} WHERE {parent_column} = <the value you saved in {column}>;
-- Create the parent first, or save the child with an existing {parent}.{parent_column}.
fk_has_children:
-- See how many rows still point to it:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {child} WHERE {column} = <the id you're deleting>;
not_null:
-- Send a value for {column}, or give the column a default:
ALTER TABLE {table} MODIFY {column} <its type> NOT NULL DEFAULT <value>;
value_too_long:
SELECT MAX(CHAR_LENGTH({column})) FROM {table};
SHOW COLUMNS FROM {table} LIKE '{column}';
ALTER TABLE {table} MODIFY {column} VARCHAR(255);  -- or TEXT for long text
out_of_range: ALTER TABLE {table} MODIFY {column} BIGINT;  -- or DECIMAL(15,2) for money
bad_value_type:
-- Send a real {column} value: numbers without commas, dates as 'YYYY-MM-DD', NULL (not '') when empty.
-- To read a date like '{value}': STR_TO_DATE('{value}', '%d-%m-%Y')
check_violation: SELECT CHECK_CLAUSE FROM information_schema.CHECK_CONSTRAINTS WHERE CONSTRAINT_NAME = '{constraint}';
-- then save a value that meets that rule
charset_mismatch:
ALTER DATABASE <db> CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
ALTER TABLE {table} CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
-- and in the app's connection: charset=utf8mb4
disk_full:
-- Common mistake: deleting binary log files with rm. The server's .index list still names them (MySQL then refuses PURGE BINARY LOGS
-- until the .index file is fixed) and a replica that still needed them breaks. Always remove them with PURGE BINARY LOGS.
out_of_memory:
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'innodb_buffer_pool_size';
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'max_connections';

-- In my.cnf, size it to the server (database-only: ~60% of RAM; shared server: much less), then restart:
innodb_buffer_pool_size = <e.g. 1G on a 4 GB shared server>
max_connections = <what the app really needs>
packet_too_large:
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'max_allowed_packet';
SET GLOBAL max_allowed_packet = 64*1024*1024;  -- also set it in my.cnf to keep it after restart
-- Better: insert in batches and keep files outside the database.
temp_space_full:
-- Add an index for the GROUP BY / ORDER BY columns of that query, then:
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'tmp_table_size'; SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'max_heap_table_size';
statement_timeout: EXPLAIN <your query>;  -- look for type = ALL and a big rows number
-- Add the index EXPLAIN is missing; paste the query here and I'll write it.
full_scan:
-- Paste the query and I'll give the exact index, e.g.:
ALTER TABLE {table} ADD INDEX idx_{table}_{column} ({column});
deadlock: SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS;  -- the LATEST DETECTED DEADLOCK section shows both transactions and the rows
-- In code: update rows in the same order (e.g. ORDER BY id) and retry the transaction when error 1213 comes back.
lock_wait:
-- Who is blocking whom:
SELECT r.trx_id waiting, r.trx_query waiting_query, b.trx_id blocking, b.trx_query blocking_query, b.trx_started
FROM information_schema.innodb_trx b JOIN performance_schema.data_lock_waits w ON w.BLOCKING_ENGINE_TRANSACTION_ID = b.trx_id
JOIN information_schema.innodb_trx r ON r.trx_id = w.REQUESTING_ENGINE_TRANSACTION_ID;
-- If a forgotten transaction blocks: KILL <its thread id>;  (after checking what it is)
serialization_failure: -- Retry the whole transaction 2-3 times with a short wait when it fails.
idle_transaction: SELECT trx_id, trx_started, trx_mysql_thread_id FROM information_schema.innodb_trx ORDER BY trx_started LIMIT 5;
-- then KILL <trx_mysql_thread_id>; and fix the code path that leaves it open
metadata_lock:
SELECT * FROM performance_schema.metadata_locks WHERE OBJECT_NAME = '{table}';
SHOW PROCESSLIST;

-- End the long transaction holding the table, then run the ALTER off-peak with:
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 5;
access_denied:
-- As an admin, check how the user exists:
SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE user = '{user}';

-- Reset the password for the host the app connects from:
ALTER USER '{user}'@'{host_pattern}' IDENTIFIED BY '<new password>';
host_not_allowed:
CREATE USER '{user}'@'{host}' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>';
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON <db>.* TO '{user}'@'{host}';
-- On cPanel hosting: Remote MySQL -> add {host}
server_unreachable:
-- On the database server:
systemctl status mysql   # is it running?
ss -ltnp | grep 3306     # is it listening, on which address?
-- For remote access, bind-address in my.cnf must not be 127.0.0.1, and the firewall must allow 3306 from the app server.
connection_lost: -- In the app: reconnect/ping before reusing an idle connection.
permission_denied: GRANT {token} ON <db>.{table} TO '{user}'@'{host}';  -- only the right that's missing
ssl_required: -- Connect with SSL, e.g. mysql --ssl-mode=REQUIRED ..., or in PHP PDO: PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_SSL_CA => '/path/ca.pem'
replica_lag:
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G   -- MySQL 8.0.22+; older MySQL and MariaDB: SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G
-- Seconds_Behind_Source = how far behind; Relay_Log_Space growing = changes arrive faster than they are applied

-- Find which of these it is, then fix that one:
-- 1) one huge UPDATE/DELETE on the primary: redo such jobs in small batches (e.g. 5,000 rows per transaction)
-- 2) tables without a PRIMARY KEY under row-based logging: every row change searches the whole table on the replica, so add a primary key
-- 3) one apply thread: use parallel apply (replica_parallel_workers; MariaDB: slave_parallel_threads)
-- 4) a weaker or busy replica (slow disk, long reports running there)
-- Reads that must see a save made a moment ago (login, checkout) should go to the primary, not the replica.
replication_stopped:
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G   -- MariaDB/older: SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G
-- Last_SQL_Errno / Last_SQL_Error (or Last_IO_Error) is the real reason; MySQL 8 also: SELECT * FROM performance_schema.replication_applier_status_by_worker\G

-- Common mistake: SET GLOBAL sql_replica_skip_counter = 1 (sql_slave_skip_counter) or slave_skip_errors as the fix.
-- Each skip throws a change away, the replica silently drifts further, and the next error comes back worse.
-- If many rows differ, rebuild the replica from a fresh backup of the primary instead.

-- Stop new drift: make the replica refuse app writes:
SET GLOBAL super_read_only = ON;   -- MySQL (MariaDB: SET GLOBAL read_only = ON;)
source_log_purged:
-- The changes the replica needs no longer exist on the primary, so it can't be repaired by restarting.
-- Safe fix: rebuild the replica from a fresh, consistent backup of the primary
-- (mysqldump --single-transaction --source-data=2, MariaDB: mariadb-dump --single-transaction --master-data=2, or a physical backup), then start replication from the position recorded in it.

-- Common mistake: pointing the replica at the next log file that still exists (CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_LOG_FILE=...).
-- It starts again, but every change in the deleted files is silently missing on the replica.

-- Before purging logs in future, check what each replica has read:
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G   -- on each replica: Source_Log_File (MariaDB: Master_Log_File)
SHOW BINARY LOGS;        -- on the primary
-- and keep logs longer than a replica could be down: binlog_expire_logs_seconds
write_on_replica: SELECT @@hostname, @@port, @@read_only, @@super_read_only;   -- read_only = 1: this server is a replica or switched to read-only

-- Send writes to the primary: check the host in the app's database config (or the writer endpoint of your cloud database).
-- After a failover, restart or recycle the app's connection pool so it stops using connections to the old primary.
-- Common mistake: SET GLOBAL read_only = OFF on a replica to make the error go away; writes there make it drift and stop replication later.
binlog_not_expiring:
SELECT @@log_bin, @@binlog_expire_logs_seconds;
SHOW BINARY LOGS;   -- how many files and how big (needs REPLICATION CLIENT / BINLOG MONITOR)

-- First check what every replica still needs: SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G on each (Source_Log_File; MariaDB: Master_Log_File).
-- Then remove only older files, and set an expiry that outlasts the slowest replica (here 7 days):
PURGE BINARY LOGS BEFORE NOW() - INTERVAL 7 DAY;
SET GLOBAL binlog_expire_logs_seconds = 604800;   -- and the same in my.cnf, or it resets on restart

-- Common mistake: rm on binary log files, or turning log_bin off to save space.
-- rm leaves the .index list and replicas out of step; log_bin off breaks replication and point-in-time restore.

unknown_table.sql: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()

unknown_column.sql: SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name = :table

resolve.sql: SELECT table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.statistics WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND index_name = :key ORDER BY seq_in_index LIMIT 1
SELECT referenced_table_name, referenced_column_name FROM information_schema.key_column_usage WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND constraint_name = :constraint LIMIT 1

value_too_long.sql: SELECT character_maximum_length FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name = :table AND column_name = :column

sql: SELECT variable_value FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE variable_name = 'Max_used_connections'

lock_wait.sql: SELECT trx_id, trx_started, trx_query FROM information_schema.innodb_trx WHERE trx_started < NOW() - INTERVAL 30 SECOND

idle_transaction.sql: SELECT trx_id, trx_started, trx_mysql_thread_id FROM information_schema.innodb_trx WHERE trx_query IS NULL AND trx_started < NOW() - INTERVAL 60 SECOND

write_on_replica.proof: this server has read_only = ON (it only accepts reads)

binlog_not_expiring.sql: SELECT 1 FROM performance_schema.global_variables v WHERE UPPER(v.variable_name) = 'LOG_BIN' AND v.variable_value = 'ON' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM performance_schema.global_variables e WHERE UPPER(e.variable_name) IN ('BINLOG_EXPIRE_LOGS_SECONDS', 'EXPIRE_LOGS_DAYS') AND e.variable_value + 0 > 0)
binlog_not_expiring.proof: binary logging is on and no expiry is set, so old binary logs are never removed

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS type), which works on every database.
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS type) likho, ye har database pe chalta hai.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS SIGNED) (MySQL/MariaDB's integer cast).
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS SIGNED) likho (MySQL/MariaDB ka integer cast).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
{db} mein :: cast nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use CAST(x AS type) with {db}'s type names (CHAR, SIGNED, DECIMAL(p,s), DATE, DATETIME).
refuses.fix_hi: CAST(x AS type) likho, {db} ke type naamon ke saath (CHAR, SIGNED, DECIMAL(p,s), DATE, DATETIME).

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein ILIKE nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use LIKE: with the usual case-insensitive (_ci) collation it already ignores case. On a _bin or _cs column, compare LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER('...').
refuses.fix_hi: LIKE likho: aam _ci collation pe ye pehle se case ignore karta hai. _bin/_cs column pe LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER('...').

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein DISTINCT ON nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: For one row per group, number the rows with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) in a subquery and keep rn = 1 (MySQL 8 / MariaDB 10.2+).
refuses.fix_hi: Har group ki ek row ke liye subquery mein ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) lagao aur rn = 1 rakho.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein NULLS LAST nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Sort on 'x IS NULL' first (false before true), then on x.
refuses.fix_hi: Pehle 'x IS NULL' pe sort karo (false pehle), phir x pe.

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein NULLS FIRST nahi hota (wo PostgreSQL ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Sort on 'x IS NOT NULL' first (NULL rows first), then on x.
refuses.fix_hi: Pehle 'x IS NOT NULL' pe sort karo (NULL rows pehle), phir x pe.

refuses.title_en: {db} has no TOP n (that's SQL Server)
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein TOP n nahi hota (wo SQL Server ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Remove TOP n and end the query with ORDER BY ... LIMIT n.
refuses.fix_hi: TOP n hatao aur query ke aakhir mein ORDER BY ... LIMIT n likho.

refuses.error: error 1305, FUNCTION GETDATE does not exist
refuses.title_hi: {db} mein GETDATE() nahi hota (wo SQL Server ka hai)
refuses.fix_en: Use NOW() (date and time) or CURDATE() (date only).
refuses.fix_hi: NOW() (date aur time) ya CURDATE() (sirf date) likho.

refuses.error: error 1305, FUNCTION STRING_AGG does not exist
refuses.title_en: {db} has no STRING_AGG() (that's PostgreSQL / SQL Server)

refuses.title_hi: {db} mein $1 placeholder nahi hote (wo PostgreSQL ke hain)
refuses.fix_en: MySQL/MariaDB drivers use ? (or named :name placeholders in PDO).
refuses.fix_hi: MySQL/MariaDB drivers ? (ya PDO mein :name) use karte hain.
